title: Modeling and Simulation Credibility Assessment of Implicit FEA for Bone Cement Mantle Crack Initiation and Creep
runhead: Credibility of Bone Cement Mantle FEA
device: Orthopedic bone cement mantle surrounding a femoral stem in cemented arthroplasty

models.name: AXI-Mantle v1.2 (Axisymmetric Segment, Implicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Time-dependent viscoelastic creep strain, principal stress, hydrostatic stress, and crack driving metrics (cohesive damage evolution, energy release rate proxies) within a 2D axisymmetric cement mantle segment with explicit stem–cement and cement–bone interfaces.

models.name: PS-Construct v0.9 (Patient-Specific 3D Construct, Implicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Spatial distributions of creep strain, multiaxial stress, interfacial tractions, and cohesive damage in a subject-specific femur–cement–stem assembly with contact, porosity-informed elastic–viscoelastic properties, and localized defects.

mechanisms.name: Monotonic crack initiation under impaction-like and early postoperative loads
mechanisms.why_it_matters: High local tractions and residual stress concentrations can nucleate microcracks in the mantle, compromising early stability and accelerating failure.

mechanisms.name: Time-dependent creep under sustained joint reaction and hoop stress
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Creep relaxation and strain accumulation can thin load paths, alter fit, and elevate interfacial stresses, predisposing the mantle to later cracking.

mechanisms.name: Creep–fatigue interaction during daily cyclic activities
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Creep-induced stress redistribution modifies fatigue hot-spots, enabling small cracks to coalesce and propagate under physiologic cycles.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest

deviation.detail: All credibility factor scores are reported on a 0–12 Evidence Rating scale with defined anchors (0, 3, 6, 9, 12) for each factor, provided separately for every model × mechanism pair.
